clue.text: Conservative 60s youths in The Carpenters

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
the flower-power young people of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that Tory-voting sixties flower children were members of the brother-and-sister pop duo The Carpenters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carpenters looks like the pop band's name, but it is a plain plural noun. Chippy is British slang for a carpenter (it is also a fish-and-chip shop).
explanation.definitionFit: Chippies is informal British slang for joiners and woodworkers, so it is a synonym for carpenters.

clue.text: During film, taxis picked up some furniture

indicators.note: taxis that picked up a fare carry it inside, so the other pieces ride within

blocks.note: cabs are taxis
in means during, as in in the night
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: While a movie is being shot, taxis collect pieces of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a sound-alike reading, but here the taxis take on passengers: CAB(IN ET)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinets are cupboards with shelves or drawers, which are items of furniture.

clue.text: Airing unfit broadcast can be very annoying

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn about

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Putting out unsuitable programmes on air can be highly irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Infuriating means making someone furious, so it is an intensified form of annoying.

clue.text: Expert with knight that's put on weight, say

blocks.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
N is the chess notation for knight
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A specialist accompanied by a knight who has gained some pounds, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Say at the end looks like the 'for example' tag, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce a word is to utter it aloud, so it is a synonym for to say.

clue.text: Weariness is often nuisance some of the time

indicators.note: only some of the text is used, so the letters sit inside the run of words

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Tiredness is frequently a bother on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of the time' reads as 'occasionally', but it signals that only part of the words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless boredom and dissatisfaction, a form of weariness.

clue.text: Small marks in thin fallen branches

blocks.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
check marks made against items on a list

explanation.surface: Someone notices tiny marks on slender twigs lying on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticks are slender pieces of wood that have dropped from trees, a direct description.

clue.text: Young child my boss carried

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
speaking as a journalist, my boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A worker's toddler was hauled around by their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is spoken in the voice of a newspaper writer, whose boss is the ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Toted is the past tense of tote, meaning to carry something heavy.

clue.text: Piece of pewter on the bottom of copper vessel

indicators.note: a piece is only a small part, here just the first letter
in a down answer, sitting on the bottom places one piece beneath the other

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bit of pewter soldered onto the base of a copper pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a small drinking vessel.

clue.text: Cheekily bold as some British special forces?

blocks.note: first meaning: impudent and spirited
second meaning, whimsical: like members of the SAS, the British Army's Special Air Service

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented adjective: SAS plus the -y ending, meaning SAS-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy describes someone lively and impertinent, which is a cheeky kind of boldness.

clue.text: Think carefully about Tory party heading for ruin

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: CON is the abbreviation for a Conservative, a Tory
a side is one party in a dispute or contest
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political commentator ponders the Conservative party heading towards disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to weigh it up and reflect on it with care.

clue.text: Fan about to be poked by old fool

indicators.note: something poked by another thing has that thing pushed into its middle, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast, as in film buff
on means about, as in a talk on birds
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An admirer is about to be jabbed by some aged idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a cooling device being poked, but it is an enthusiast; the old letter goes inside the word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon is a clownish, ridiculous person, a close synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Month's work for heavily-armed marine type?

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
an opus is a work, especially a musical composition

explanation.surface: A month's labour required for a heavily equipped soldier of the marines.
explanation.walkthrough: Marine type looks like a Royal Marine, and heavily-armed like weapons; the question mark flags that the arms are eight tentacles on a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The octopus is a sea creature with eight limbs, so it is playfully heavily-armed and a marine animal.

clue.text: Actors in cast snorting cocaine and downers

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about or moulded afresh, so the words are reshaped
snorting a drug takes it in through the nose, so one letter is drawn inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A showbiz scandal: members of the cast taking cocaine and sedatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actors' and 'cast' both suggest the theatre, but cast is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs that dull the senses and induce sleep, and downers is slang for such sedatives.

clue.text: Deterioration in city comes in time

indicators.note: one thing coming in to another enters it, so it sits inside

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, a crossword stand-in for city
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Urban decline arrives in a town given enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the London postal district covering the City, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Decay is gradual rotting or decline, so it means deterioration.

clue.text: Bit of sauce in pic cheeses off board members

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the first letter
food gone off has spoiled, so the letters are rearranged as if ruined

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A smear of sauce on a photo of cheeses that have spoiled, served on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: Board members looks like company directors, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are the kings, rooks, pawns and others that stand on the chessboard, so they are literally its members.

clue.text: Coach or caravan

blocks.note: first meaning: to instruct or tutor someone
second meaning: a line of travellers or pack animals in procession

explanation.walkthrough: Coach and caravan both look like road vehicles; one is a verb for teaching and the other a convoy of camels or wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to coach, and a train is a long procession of people, vehicles or animals, like a caravan.

clue.text: Was The Go-between thought to lack central character?

indicators.note: lacking its central character means the one letter in the exact middle of the word is dropped

blocks.note: to meditate is to think deeply, so thought in the past tense

explanation.surface: A question about whether the novel The Go-Between was considered to have no strong protagonist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Go-Between is L. P. Hartley's novel, but here it is just a role: someone acting as a go-between. MEDITATED has nine letters, and its fifth, a T, goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mediated acted as an intermediary between two sides, which is exactly what a go-between does.

clue.text: Mollify one in Cambridge Uni scandal?

indicators.note: in tells us one item is placed inside the other words

blocks.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
I is the Roman numeral for one
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Can a scandal at a Cambridge university be smoothed over by one person?
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge Uni looks English, but this is the American Cambridge. The I sits in MIT-GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to make less severe, and to mollify is to soothe or soften, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Type primarily involved in transformative trauma op?

definitions.text: Type primarily involved in transformative trauma op?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken
a thing involved in another is caught up inside it
something transformative changes the shape of what follows, so the letters are remade

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A description of the kind of surgeon who carries out a life-changing emergency operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a person whose operation removes a limb is transformative.
explanation.definitionFit: An amputator is someone who cuts off a limb, a surgical procedure often needed after severe injury.

clue.text: Writhing serpents which might be found under tree

definitions.text: which might be found under tree

indicators.note: writhing means twisting and contorting, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Snakes coiling about that might be found lurking beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a Christmas tree, not one in a jungle with snakes beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Presents are gifts traditionally placed beneath the Christmas tree.

clue.text: I'd reviewed Man of God for Yelena Popovic, say

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at again from the other end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the contraction taken as its two letters
a rector is a member of the clergy in charge of a parish

explanation.surface: Someone says they wrote a review of a film about a clergyman, perhaps for its maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Man of God is the title of Yelena Popovic's 2021 film about Saint Nektarios, which makes 'reviewed' look like film criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelena Popovic is a filmmaker, so she is an example of a person who directs films.

clue.text: Tough question model put to Republican leader

indicators.note: put to means placed against, so one piece is set beside the next
a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: to pose is what a model does for a photographer or artist
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A difficult question put by a fashion model to the head of the Republican party.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling problem, a hard question that is difficult to answer.

clue.text: Wind up in trough, slipping close to farm

indicators.note: something slipping falls away, so a letter is lost from the word
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: a manger is a feeding trough for animals
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone ends up falling into a feeding trough on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind up is British slang for annoy, used as a verb here; the M at the front of MANGER slips away.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up is to deliberately irritate them, so it is a synonym for to anger.

clue.text: Signs there has been a fire in trees

definitions.text: Signs there has been a fire

blocks.clueFragment: Signs there has been a fire
blocks.note: first meaning: the powdery remains left after burning
second meaning: a kind of deciduous tree, in the plural

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as evidence of a forest fire; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is the grey residue after burning, and the ash is a common woodland tree of the olive family.

clue.text: Violent attack that bishop is involved in

indicators.note: one involved in something is caught up inside it

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A savage assault that a churchman takes part in.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means fanatical or furious, as well as infected with rabies, so it is a synonym for violent.

clue.text: Singers cut No.6, 7 and 9 from compilation album

indicators.note: cutting numbered items from something removes the letters at those positions in the word

blocks.note: a greatest hits album collects an artist's best-known songs

explanation.surface: A record company drops tracks six, seven and nine from a best-of collection by some vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Singers looks like the performers on the album, but it means songbirds. Removing letters six, seven and nine of GREATESTHITS (E, S, H) leaves GREAT TITS.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common European songbird, so great tits are birds that sing.

clue.text: Tunnel vision hampers The King

indicators.note: a hamper is a basket, so the words hold the letters inside them

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Narrow-mindedness holds back the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was nicknamed The King of Rock and Roll, often simply The King.

clue.text: Swimmer and boxer spotted in hotel bar

indicators.note: someone spotted in a place is seen inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer
bar and but both mean except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: An athlete and a famous fighter are seen in a hotel's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotel bar reads as a place to drink, but it splits: H holds ALI, and bar means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A halibut is a large flatfish, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: The Parisian scoffing ravioli ultimately's porky

indicators.note: scoffing means eating greedily, so one letter is swallowed inside
ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: le is French for the
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Parisian gobbling down pasta parcels is fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Porky looks like an adjective for overweight, but it is British rhyming slang: pork pie means a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Porky, short for pork pie, is rhyming slang for an untruth.

clue.text: One found in two containers in Roman palace

indicators.note: a thing found in another is located inside it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the first container: a vat is a large tank
the second container: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: One item is discovered in a pair of storage boxes in a palace in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two containers' supplies two separate words, and the one sits inside only the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the papal palace in Rome and the seat of the Pope.

clue.text: Spot to cross west-flowing river rapid

indicators.note: in an across answer, flowing west means running right to left, backwards
to cross something here is to straddle it, so the outer word goes around

blocks.note: to spy is to spot or catch sight of
the Dee, a river in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a place to ford a fast-flowing river that runs west.
explanation.walkthrough: Rapid looks like a noun for white water, but it is the adjective fast; the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy means fast or quick, a direct synonym of rapid.

clue.text: Supporters of a Russian monarchy stir TASS up

indicators.note: things that are stirred up are mixed and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Monarchists agitate the Russian state news agency, TASS.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; up alone does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarists backed the rule of the tsar, the emperor of Russia, so they supported its monarchy.
